instrument: RIPE Atlas one-off sslcert (SNI), probes chosen for maximum country coverage: 178 probes in 177 countries; reconciled against per-pointer fetch

exception.public_note: On 25 August 2026 this endpoint presented a certificate for its own name to none of the 178 probes in 177 countries: 177 saw a certificate for another name, which is withheld, and 1 saw none. Its operator was notified on 25 August 2026. On 30 September 2026 the same host presented a certificate for its own name over HTTPS, valid from 3 September 2026; the pointer the EU list of trusted lists declares for it is still http://.

methodology: A bare TLS probe with no SNI reports a CDN's default certificate as a defect; even with SNI, cloud routing can hand a default certificate to some vantages. Every figure here reconciles the Atlas run against a fetch of each pointer's actual URL. After reconciliation, on 25 August 2026, exactly one endpoint failed from every country and every method; all others validated when fetched the way software fetches them, with SNI.

correction.what: control.valid, control.probes and exception.probes held country counts under probe names (165 of 177; 177). They now hold probe counts as the RIPE Atlas API reports them (166 of 178; 178), and the country counts sit under countries and countries_own_name. reach.continents gains the 177th country (Other: 1). The exception is no longer gated and its note no longer says the operator will be notified: it was notified on 25 August 2026. The methodology is dated and in the past tense.
correction.valid_means: probes whose leaf certificate named the host. Atlas sslcert records the certificate a server presents; it does not validate the chain. The key is kept because existing readers use it; own_name holds the same count.
correction.no_answer_means: probes that received no certificate (timeouts and TLS alerts).
